Repository: Textualize/rich

Issue:
Handle graphemes

Rich has never handled multi-codepoint emoji, because terminals were highly inconsistent about how they were rendered. And there was no way to know in advance how wide a given collection of codepoints was going to be. 

This is technically still the case. However modern terminals are more consistent now, and they tend to follow unicode rules. Which means that Rich can also follow those rules and get it right more of the time.

This PR uses the data from https://github.com/jquast/wcwidth to calculate widths in the same way. I didn't use wcwidth directly, as Rich has more complex requirements. Calculating the width of a string is not enough, if you want to do wrapping, cropping etc.

This PR adds the capability to split strings in to sequences that produce a single glyph in the terminal. And that is used in a few low-level functions.

The data is stored in a way that keeps startup time low, and makes width calculations more optimal than wcwidth.

This iteration should hopefully offer similar performance to the earlier versions. In the nearish future there will be a Rust library to speed up some of the lower level operations.

Fixes https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3897

The issue description states that Rich needs to handle multi-codepoint emoji by splitting strings into sequences that produce a single glyph in the terminal, following Unicode rules for width calculation.

The file `rich/cells.py` contains functions related to cell width calculation, specifically `get_character_cell_size` and `cell_len`. The description mentions that this capability is used in a few low-level functions.

The candidate locations provided by the system are:

5. `rich/progress.py::Task.time_remaining`

Since the core issue is about correctly calculating widths for multi-codepoint characters (graphemes), `rich/cells.py::get_character_cell_size` is the most relevant function to investigate for changes to support grapheme splitting/width calculation.

I will check `rich/cells.py` for any existing logic that might need modification to handle grapheme boundaries instead of just codepoint boundaries.

The existing `get_character_cell_size` function takes a single character (`str`) and returns its cell size (0, 1, or 2). This implies it operates on single Unicode codepoints. To handle graphemes, it would need to operate on a sequence of codepoints that form a single visual unit.

Given the context of the PR description ("This PR adds the capability to split strings in to sequences that produce a single glyph in the terminal"), the change likely involves introducing a function or modifying existing ones to iterate over graphemes instead of characters/codepoints when calculating width or splitting text.

I will focus on `rich/cells.py::get_character_cell_size` as the most likely place where the logic for determining character width needs to be updated to respect grapheme boundaries.
